{{Recipe}}

'''Ful medames''' is a traditional Sudanese dish made from cooked fava beans, commonly enjoyed for breakfast or as a light meal. It is a nutritious and filling dish, packed with protein and fiber. The beans are typically seasoned with olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, and a blend of spices, resulting in a flavorful and satisfying culinary experience.

== Ingredients ==

* 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] dried [[Cookbook:Fava Bean|fava beans]]
* 4 cups water (for soaking)
* 4 cups water (for cooking)
* 4 cloves [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* ¼ cup extra-virgin [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
* Juice of 1 [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] ground [[Cookbook:Cumin|cumin]]
* ½ teaspoon ground [[Cookbook:Coriander|coriander]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]], to taste
* Optional toppings: [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]], [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]] [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]], chopped [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]], [[Cookbook:Hard Cooked Eggs|hard-boiled eggs]], [[Cookbook:Feta Cheese|feta cheese]]

== Equipment ==

* Large pot
* [[Cookbook:Colander|Colander]] or [[Cookbook:Sieve|strainer]]
* [[Cookbook:Mixing Bowl|Mixing bowl]]
* Wooden spoon or [[Cookbook:Spatula|spatula]]
* Serving dish

== Procedure ==

# Rinse the dried fava beans under cold water and then place them in a large pot. Add 4 cups of water to the pot and let the beans soak overnight, or for at least 8 hours. This helps soften the beans and reduce the cooking time.
# Drain the soaked fava beans and rinse them under cold water. Return the beans to the pot and add 4 cups of fresh water. Bring the water to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] over medium-high heat. Once boiling, reduce the heat to low and let the beans [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for about 1–1½ hours, or until they become tender. Stir occasionally and skim off any foam that forms on the surface.
# Once the beans are tender, drain them using a colander or strainer and transfer them to a mixing bowl. Add minced garlic, extra-virgin olive oil, lemon juice, ground cumin, ground coriander, and salt to the bowl. Mix everything together, ensuring that the beans are coated evenly with the seasoning.
# For a smoother consistency, you can use a fork or a potato masher to lightly mash some of the beans. This step is optional and can be adjusted according to your preference.
# Transfer the seasoned ful medames to a serving dish. Ful medames can be enjoyed warm or at room temperature. You can serve it with a variety of optional toppings such as chopped parsley, diced tomatoes, chopped onions, hard-boiled eggs, or crumbled feta cheese. It is commonly served with bread or as a side dish alongside other Sudanese specialties.

steps.text: Rinse the dried fava beans under cold water and then place them in a large pot. Add 4 cups of water to the pot and let the beans soak overnight, or for at least 8 hours. This helps soften the beans and reduce the cooking time.

Drain the soaked fava beans and rinse them under cold water. Return the beans to the pot and add 4 cups of fresh water. Bring the water to a boil over medium-high heat. Once boiling, reduce the heat to low and let the beans simmer for about 1–1½ hours, or until they become tender. Stir occasionally and skim off any foam that forms on the surface.

Once the beans are tender, drain them using a colander or strainer and transfer them to a mixing bowl. Add minced garlic, extra-virgin olive oil, lemon juice, ground cumin, ground coriander, and salt to the bowl. Mix everything together, ensuring that the beans are coated evenly with the seasoning.
For a smoother consistency, you can use a fork or a potato masher to lightly mash some of the beans. This step is optional and can be adjusted according to your preference.

Transfer the seasoned ful medames to a serving dish. Ful medames can be enjoyed warm or at room temperature. You can serve it with a variety of optional toppings such as chopped parsley, diced tomatoes, chopped onions, hard-boiled eggs, or crumbled feta cheese. It is commonly served with bread or as a side dish alongside other Sudanese specialties.
